audit:Reference-data read path: faci.summary:
The shared facility table and its live overlays are read in at least 9 places, on 6 different refresh clocks. The main map endpoint (/infrastructures) caches nothing at all and rebuilds everything on every request. Recommendations deep-copy all 1,682 rows on each request. Nothing invalidates caches when the process itself writes. The worst stability hazards are:
- (a) Any failure of the latest-congestion RPC turns into 1,682 parallel thread calls. Simulated on the real 16-worker executor, that blocks every Supabase call and every DNS lookup in the process for about 14s.
- (b) Facility pagination has no ORDER BY in the hot paths, and facility_source_refs is read in one capped request.
- (c) The web fallback that the map usually takes today is silently capped at 1,000 rows by PostgREST.

**Design: one in-process read model (`app/services/reference_snapshot.py`)**
- **Base layer (changes minutes to days).** A frozen snapshot holding: all rows as explicit columns, including inactive ones; an `active` tuple; `by_id`; a coarse grid index; and today's tourism priors plus place_data_source baked in. It is rebuilt when the data changes, found by a 60s probe of count + max(updated_at) (updated_at is trigger-maintained, init.sql:90), or when the KST date rolls over.
- **LiveOverlay (changes seconds to minutes).** Raw latest congestion rows, unexpired corroborated availability, and active timesales. It is refreshed every 60s. Each overlay records `next_flip_at`, the earliest moment a 30-min is_current, 24h is_stale, expiry or sale boundary flips, so baked bytes are rebuilt exactly then.
- **Derived artifacts, rebuilt per version, never per request:**
  - the /infrastructures bytes. Rows are validated once through InfrastructureItem, bad rows are dropped and logged instead of failing the whole response, and bytes come from `TypeAdapter(list[InfrastructureItem]).dump_json`. The ETag is a blake2b hash of the body.
  - the /congestion/estimates bytes.
  - a slim map view and a detail view.
- **Refresh mechanics.** One refresher task, started in lifespan, owns every source:
  - It is single-flight by construction and runs loads in a dedicated 1-thread executor.
  - On failure it keeps the last good copy, with 5s→300s backoff.
  - It publishes by atomic reference swap. Readers take `snap = current()` once per request.
- **Immediate updates on in-process writes.** Every in-process writer calls `mark_dirty()`, debounced about 1s, so reports, admin override, simulate_peak, merchant seat and timesale changes, and admin/dev/search facility writes show up at once. Writers outside the process are bounded by the 60s probe. This assumes the single uvicorn worker, as today.
- **ResponseCache keys** gain `(base.version, overlay.version)`, so cached responses are replaced when the data changes rather than on a TTL.

**Measurements (synthetic data calibrated to the prod profile, py3.11 on this desktop)**
- **App-side CPU of the current /infrastructures path is only about 40ms.** That is PostgREST parse 13ms + 1,682 models 9ms + response_model re-validation 5ms + json.dumps 11ms. The 2-4s is I/O: at least 4 dependent round-trip stages from Render in Oregon to Supabase in Seoul, about 2MB downloaded, and about 16 thread hops per call.
- **Pre-serialized version:**
  - one-time build cost is about 16ms plus a 3ms hash.
  - per-request cost is about 1µs to construct the Response.
  - the output is json-equal to the current FastAPI response (verified).
- **Other costs:**
  - deep-copying 1,682 rows takes 27ms and about 5-6MB each time.
  - tourism prior attachment takes 33ms per call.
  - the slim map view is 62% smaller (gzip 61%).

**Contract safety**
- Keeping `@router.get(..., response_model=list[InfrastructureItem])` and returning a starlette Response leaves the OpenAPI snapshot unchanged (verified locally). FastAPI skips validation for a Response returned directly ([FastAPI: Return a Response Directly](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/response-directly/)).
- ETag revalidation works with no web change, because api-client.ts:252 uses the default fetch cache mode.
- score.py and the SPOT weights are untouched. score.py already copies `features` before mutating it (score.py:59-62).
- Render's load balancer already applies Brotli/gzip ([Render compression Q&A](https://community.render.com/t/do-you-automatically-compress-json-responses-with-brotli/5477)), so gzipping in-process is optional.
- render.yaml has no region, so the service runs in `oregon` ([Render Blueprint spec](https://render.com/docs/blueprint-spec)), and region cannot be changed on an existing service ([Render regions](https://render.com/docs/regions)).

**Phasing, most stability gained per unit of risk first**
- **P0 (small patches, today):**
  - delete the per-facility fan-out fallback.
  - add `.order("id")` or keyset pagination to `fetch_active_facilities` and safety.
  - paginate facility_source_refs.
- **P1:** snapshot plus pre-serialized /infrastructures with ETag and 304, with the contract unchanged; plus the write hooks.
- **P2:** move the reco, course, predict, safety, estimator, report and parking_derived consumers onto the snapshot. Delete facility_cache.py and 5 private loaders.
- **P3:** event-driven parking and estimates, published by the 10-min collect; the slim /infrastructures/map plus /infrastructures/detail/{id} with the web switch-over; the Singapore region move (a human task).

**Resulting cost:** steady memory of about 7-9MB for the snapshot, replacing about 6-7MB of existing caches. Per-request transients go away: 17-25MB per map call and about 5MB per reco call. The map, recommendations and estimates also read one consistent version instead of five.

Scratch benchmarks used: C:\Users\hennr\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-hennr-Desktop-NEXTSPOT\bb3f89c1-647b-4048-ad72-33f0ad33fdd6\scratchpad\bench_infra.py, bench_break.py, bench_ta.py, bench_prior.py, bench_est.py, fanout.py and fa_resp.py (the Response/OpenAPI verification). The repo was not modified. A relevant pytest subset passed: 43 tests.

findings.title: /infrastructures rebuilds the whole map on every request: 4 dependent Seoul round-trip stages, ~16 thread hops, 17-25MB transient, no cache. Replace it with one immutable reference snapshot plus pre-serialized bytes and an ETag.
findings.evidence:
- **No cache on this endpoint:** routers/infrastructures.py:370-440. docs/SYSTEM_MAP.md:255 wrongly lists facility_cache for /main.
- **Rows:** :395 calls fetch_active_facilities('*'). At :268-270, fetch_all_rows fetches 2 offset pages serially in one thread (core/supabase.py:373-386). :280-283 then reads the whole facility_source_refs table.
- **Overlays:** :401-404 gathers the RPC with 1,682 ids (:313-318) and availability in 12 chunks of 150 (availability_service.py:51,82-86), each chunk its own asyncio.to_thread (:57).
- **Serialization:** :406-433 builds 1,682 pydantic models, which response_model (:370) then re-validates.
- **Not memory-gated:** memory_guard.py:78-89 does not cover this route.
- **Web side:** the client gives up after 4000ms (apps/web/app/main/page.tsx:597-605). useCongestionAlerts.ts:30,169-177 re-downloads the full map every 3 min per tab with notifications enabled.
- **Executor:** the default executor has 16 threads (main.py:39).
- **Region:** render.yaml:5-12 sets no region, so the service runs in Oregon while Supabase is in Seoul.
findings.cost:
- **Given measurements:** 2.0-2.7s locally, 2.7-4.2s prod TTFB, and +17-25MB transient heap per request. My calibrated synthetic run traced a 22MB peak, which matches.
- **CPU is small:** app-side CPU is only ~40ms on the desktop (parse 13 + models 9 + response_model 5 + json.dumps 11ms), est. 150-250ms on 0.5 CPU.
- **Latency is I/O:** ≥4 dependent trans-Pacific stages plus ~2MB download. Supabase connections expire after 15s idle (core/supabase.py:42), so sporadic map loads often start on fresh connections that pay TCP slow start (est. several RTTs per MB).
- **Executor pressure:** one call holds up to 13-15 of the 16 executor threads, so two concurrent map loads queue every other to_thread call and every httpx DNS lookup.
- **Pre-serialized alternative (measured):**
  - one-time build: models 10ms + dump_json 6ms + blake2b 3ms.
  - per request: Response(bytes) ≈1µs, 0 DB calls, 0 thread hops, no transient heap.
  - a 304 carries no body.
  - the output is json-equal to today's FastAPI response.
findings.proposal:
**Add `app/services/reference_snapshot.py`.**

- **Data layout.** A frozen `FacilityBase` holds:
  - `version` (hash of the canonical source bytes), `kst_date`
  - `all_rows: tuple[dict]` (explicit columns), `active: tuple`, `by_id: MappingProxyType`, a coarse-grid index
  - today's priors and place_data_source baked in.

  A `LiveOverlay` holds raw latest-congestion rows, availability, timesales and `next_flip_at`. A `MapPayload` holds `etag`, `body` and an optional `body_gz`, keyed by `(base.version, overlay.version, flip_epoch, normalized params)`.
- **Refresh.** One refresher task started in lifespan:
  - base: probes count + max(updated_at) every 60s and rebuilds when it changes.
  - overlay: refreshes every 60s, and also at `next_flip_at`, because is_current (30 min) and is_stale (24h) are baked into the bytes.
  - both: rebuild immediately on `mark_dirty()`.
  - Builds run in a dedicated 1-thread executor, keep last-good on error with backoff, and publish by atomic reference swap.
- **Serving get_infrastructures.** Keep the decorator unchanged so the OpenAPI snapshot is identical.
  - Look up bytes by normalized params. The canonical key (the web's REGION.bounds from lib/region.ts:12, and 'no params') is prebuilt eagerly.
  - Any other bbox/type filters snapshot rows and serializes once into an LRU of 4 entries.
  - Return 304 when `If-None-Match` matches. Otherwise return `Response(body, media_type='application/json')` with headers `ETag`, `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and `X-Snapshot-Age`.
  - Because the ETag is a content hash, it stays the same across OOM restarts, so browser caches keep revalidating to 304.
- **Cold start.** Lifespan runs `build_initial()` with a 20s bound. Until a snapshot exists, requests await the in-flight build for up to 3s, then return 503. The web already falls back on 503.
- **Verification.** Add a golden test comparing the old builder with the snapshot bytes (json-equal), and a test that the OpenAPI snapshot is unchanged.

findings.title: A single latest-congestion RPC error fans out into 1,682 unbounded thread calls, stalling the process for ~14s
findings.evidence:
- **Trigger:** routers/infrastructures.py:333-334 catches *any* exception from the RPC. The 09-26 ConnectionTerminated bursts (HANDOVER.md:208-211) are exactly such errors.
- **Fan-out:** :335 then runs `asyncio.gather(*[_fetch_latest_one(fid) for fid in facility_ids])` with no semaphore. Each call is its own `asyncio.to_thread` PostgREST request (:201-213).
- **Callers that pass every facility:** /infrastructures (:402), POST /predict/batch (predict.py:122) and /admin/safety/status (safety.py:110).
findings.cost:
- **Simulated with the real executor (16 workers) and 130ms per call** (scratchpad/fanout.py): 1,682 calls took 13.8s, and an unrelated to_thread call started 100ms later waited 13.7s instead of 0.13s.
- **Effect:** one transient error stalls every Supabase read, model call and httpx DNS lookup in the process for ~14s. During an incident, the calls to Supabase are multiplied 1,682×, like a retry storm.
- /health survives only because it is async.
findings.proposal:
- **Delete the fallback.** The RPC has been deployed since 20260715130000, redefined up to 20260908120000.
- In the snapshot, a failed overlay refresh keeps last-good and backs off.
- If a fallback for a missing function (PGRST202) is still wanted, make it one table query (`congestion_logs` with the same tier/source filters, ordered by facility_id, timestamp desc), never one request per facility.
- **P0 patch now:** re-raise, or return {} and log, instead of fanning out.
findings.makes_unnecessary: `_fetch_latest_one` (infrastructures.py:201-228) and the gather fallback (:333-336)
findings.stability_risk_of_change: **Low.** Worst case, the congestion overlay stays at last-good, or is empty on a cold start, instead of stalling the whole process.

findings.title: Facility pagination has no ORDER BY in the hot paths, and facility_source_refs is read in one capped, unordered request
findings.evidence:
- **Unordered filters:** fetch_active_facilities `_filters` only adds `eq('is_active', True)` (infrastructures.py:262-265), with no order. fetch_all_rows paginates by offset `range()` over separate HTTP requests, i.e. separate transactions (core/supabase.py:373-386). safety.py:76-80 does the same.
- **Consumers:** the map, the recommendation cache (recommendations.py:229) and predict (predict.py:98).
- **The repo already knows the fix:** admin.py:598 ('range 페이지 경계 고정'), infrastructures.py:622 ('전순서 보장') and parking_derived_congestion_service.py:305.
- **Refs:** facility_source_refs is read with a single `.execute()`, no pagination and no order (infrastructures.py:280-283). PostgREST caps responses at 1000 rows, per the repo's own notes at industry_baseline.py:108-110 and ingest_localdata.py:98-99.
findings.cost:
- **Plausible, not observed.** 1,682 rows means 2 pages. If an UPDATE relocates a tuple between the two page requests, one facility can be duplicated and another dropped. Such updates include the merchant seat broadcast (a features merge, merchant.py:539), the daily ingest upsert of every row, and the kakao batches.
- **Long-lived impact:** recommendations cache that result for up to 900s (facility_cache.py:14), so a facility can vanish from recommendations for 15 min.
- **Refs impact:** once localdata refs exceed 1000, place_data_source and data_updated_at for an arbitrary subset silently revert to 'tourapi'/'kakao'. That attribution is shown on cards (RecommendationCard.tsx:992).
findings.proposal:
- **Snapshot loader:** facilities with keyset pagination (`.order('id').gt('id', last).limit(1000)`), which is robust to concurrent UPDATEs; refs the same way with `source=eq.localdata`, as ingest_localdata.py:111-115 does.
- **Better (optional):** one SQL function returning json_agg of the explicit columns plus refs in a single statement. That is MVCC-consistent, has no max-rows cap and needs 1 round trip. It requires a new migration, build_reset.mjs and a PRELUDE DROP entry per AGENTS.md, and the code should fall back to keyset when PGRST202 is returned.
- **P0 patch now:** add `.order('id')` in `_filters` and in safety.py:79, and read refs with fetch_all_rows.
findings.makes_unnecessary: the unordered offset reads in fetch_active_facilities, safety._fetch_facilities and predict._fetch_facilities_id_type
findings.stability_risk_of_change: **Low.** Ordering and keyset pagination only affect page boundaries.

findings.title: In-process writes never invalidate facility data: invalidate_facility_cache has 0 callers, and TTL caches stack
findings.evidence:
- **Unused invalidation:** facility_cache.py:138-144 defines invalidate_facility_cache, and nothing in app/ calls it.
- **In-process writers of facility rows:**
  - admin.py:128, 148, 165 (create, update, delete)
  - dev.py:666 (insert)
  - merchant.py:539 (features.seat_status)
  - search.py:463-475 (upsert)
- **Stale reads:** merchant_boost.py:130-165 reads seat_status from the cached rows served by fetch_all_facilities (recommendations.py:273-281).
- **TTLs:** the soft TTL of 180s is refreshed only when a request arrives (facility_cache.py:112-118); the hard TTL is 900s. The by-type ResponseCache adds another 180s on top (response_cache.py:49, recommendations.py:939-941).
findings.cost:
- A merchant seat broadcast is valid for 30 min (merchant_boost.py:34). It is invisible to /recommendations, /by-type and /courses for at least 180s, and up to ~6 min with the response cache: roughly 10-20% of its validity, right in the demo flow.
- A deleted or deactivated facility is still recommended for up to 15 min.
- Freshness depends on traffic timing.
findings.proposal:
- **Write-through versioning:** after each successful write, call `reference_snapshot.mark_dirty('facilities'|'congestion'|'availability'|'timesales')`. The refresher debounces for ~1s, so simulate_peak's 4 chunk inserts cause one rebuild, then republishes.
- **Versioned response caches:** add `(base.version, overlay.version)` to the ResponseCache keys for by-type and courses, so cached responses end exactly when their inputs change.
- **Writers outside the process** (ingest.yml, translate_overviews.py, localdata/kakao batches, SQL Editor) are caught by the 60s probe: `facilities?select=updated_at&order=updated_at.desc&limit=1` with `count=exact` (updated_at comes from the trigger at init.sql:90-91) plus max(updated_at) of refs.
findings.makes_unnecessary: TTL guessing (FACILITY_CACHE_SOFT_TTL and TTL constants) and invalidate_facility_cache
findings.stability_risk_of_change: **Low.** The hooks are additive. A forgotten hook degrades to ≤60s staleness, which is still better than today.

- **All writers of these tables are in-process:**
  - availability: reports.py:184 (RPC)
  - congestion: reports.py:271, admin.py:237, infrastructures.py:675, merchant.py:598
  - timesales: merchant.py:309, 359, 379

- The map alone makes 12 availability requests.

findings.proposal:
**Add a LiveOverlay to the snapshot**, refreshed every 60s and immediately on `mark_dirty` from the writers above:
- **Availability:** one query, `evidence_tier=eq.corroborated&expires_at=gt.<now>&order=reported_at.desc`. No IN list; the table is tiny.
- **Congestion:** the existing RPC once per refresh with the snapshot ids, or a new zero-arg RPC. Store the raw rows and compute is_current / is_stale at read time with the wall clock via congestion_evidence.measurement_is_current, so semantics stay exact.

  - `snap.congestion_for(ids, now)`, `snap.availability_for(ids, now)` and `snap.timesales_for(ids, now)` return exactly today's dict shapes, so call sites barely change.
  - `snap.facility(id)` falls back to the DB only for ids that are not in the snapshot.

findings.title: Parking data is ingested twice and estimates are recomputed on a request-driven TTL; make both event-driven and pre-serialized
findings.evidence:
- **Collection runs in this process:** pg_cron's 10-minute collect calls area_demand.py:143-158 → area_demand_snapshot_service.py:89-91 → parking_demand_service.fetch_current_gyeongju_parking_snapshot (:297-324). That makes a fresh ITS list request plus one detail request per lot (:238-294).
- **Second, independent ITS fetch:** parking_demand_service keeps its own stale-while-revalidate cache with a 5-min realtime TTL (:30-31, :394-403, :472-516), which feeds get_nearby_parking_signal (area_demand_service.py:141-145).
- **Estimator re-reads from the DB:** it pulls back the same lots from the DB (congestion_estimator_service.py:473-486, 2 round trips), behind a request-driven lock with a 300s / 60s TTL (:88-91, :517-537). It also has its own facility cache and queries forecasts on every compute (:391-410).
- **Per-request model rebuild:** /congestion/estimates rebuilds ~800 CongestionEstimate models on every request (infrastructures.py:563-595).
findings.cost:
- ITS is hit on two unrelated schedules, each with ~N+1 HTTPS requests.
- Each recompute costs 3-5 DB round trips.
- The first request after the TTL waits up to 3s (reco, congestion_evidence.py:28) or 8s (map, infrastructures.py:540), and silently drops estimates when it times out.
- Estimates lag a fresh collect by up to 5 min, or get recomputed with no new data.

audit:Area demand / parking / Seoul.summary:
WHY GET /area-demand/forecast TAKES ~3s: a cold call makes one DB round trip that dominates the time. For every new ~100m grid key (round(lat,3), round(lng,3)), `_load_points` (area_demand_forecast_service.py:558-581) calls the plpgsql RPC `area_demand_points_near` (migration 20260904120000:114-188). That RPC recomputes the whole 56-day history of the ~4 live ITS lots inside 2km: haversine plus numeric round per lot-row, to_char per point, then jsonb_agg of up to 8,064 points. My synthetic run with the prod shape (4 lots x 144 buckets/day x 56 days) gives a payload of 427KB raw, 112KB gzip. All the Python work together takes about 40ms on the desktop: json.loads 1.7ms, `_points_from_payload` about 8ms (this part runs on the event loop, line 555), `_SeriesIndex.build` 2.4ms, the indexed forecast 0.04ms, and the backtest 25ms. So 90% or more of the ~3s is the RPC itself: DB compute on the free tier plus payload transfer. It also crosses the Pacific if Render runs in its default region: render.yaml sets no `region`, and Render's default is Oregon (https://render.com/docs/free). A warm call costs under 1ms, but it only stays warm for 5 minutes per grid (_POINTS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, line 129), while the data changes every 10 minutes. So most real visits are cold. /waiting then sends 6 sequential calls for REGION.center (apps/web/lib/areaDemandCurve.ts:50-67). Courses prefetch 12-36 cold grids per request (courses.py:680-700, 6 in parallel), which I estimate at 5-15MB of JSON pulled per cold course, plus about 1MB kept in memory per grid.

WORK REDONE ON EVERY REQUEST THAT ONLY NEEDS DOING ONCE PER 10-MINUTE COLLECTION:
(a) Re-aggregating 56 days of lot rows per grid, every 5 minutes, in the DB. Only one new snapshot arrives per 10 minutes.
(b) Re-parsing 8,064 points into Python objects and re-interning them, per grid per 5 minutes.
(c) The 28-day backtest per grid, redone every time a new snapshot changes the cache key (line 959-964).
(d) A separate live ITS fetch every 5 minutes (parking_demand_service.py:394-403), apart from the collector's own 10-minute fetch of the same upstream (297-324).
(e) Calibration state and report rebuilt on read, with 26 PostgREST round trips.
(f) The watchdog's reliability query.

The source data is tiny: about 8,064 snapshots x 4 lots = 32K (total, available) pairs. Stored as uint16 columns plus int64 timestamps that is 276KB (measured). From that store, one location's series takes 0.195ms with numpy or 3.5ms in pure Python, and it is bit-identical to the reference `aggregate_nearby_points` (verified). The 09-04 move to the RPC fixed a representation problem (52MB of dict rows) by pushing compute to the DB. Storing the data compactly fixes it at the root: 0.3MB for all grids, no RPC at all.

HANDOVER 'GridSeries -74MB' IDEA: correct but local. Measured cost per grid today: about 0.75MB of points+index at the full window, 1.16MB counting level-intern growth. At the 96-grid cap that is 72-109MB, and it keeps growing until the 56-day window fills around 2026-10-15 (history started 08-20). GridSeries would turn this into roughly 96 x 70KB, but it keeps the per-grid RPC, the TTL mismatch, the locks and the prefetch plumbing. The lot matrix (finding 1) replaces it and needs about the same consumer rewrite.

UNBOUNDED OR OVERSIZED CACHES:
- `_points_locks` (line 141/573) is truly unbounded. Keys come from users through the public unauthenticated endpoint; measured 212B per key.
- `_points_cache` is bounded by entry count but not by bytes (72-109MB).
- `_series_indexes` is bounded together with it.
- `_quality_cache` is bounded (256 small dicts) and fine.
- `_window_minutes` is an lru_cache(maxsize=None) holding 3.2MB (measured).
- `_level_intern` does nothing useful: 16,126 entries after 2 grids, i.e. about 0 sharing.
- engine-validation summary: latent but large. It reads `fcst` jsonb for each row: 28d x 5 areas = 20,160 rows, about 40MB JSON and about 130MB of Python objects (measured synthetically). The Seoul table is still at 0 rows, so this has not happened yet.

OTHER EVIDENCE:
- area-demand-alert: 3 of the last 12 runs failed (exit 22 twice, exit 1 once; GitHub API annotations). Its 'hourly' cron actually fires every 3-6 hours.
- The subsystem pytest subset passes: 170 tests.
- Outside library facts: Seoul population-only endpoint (https://data.seoul.go.kr/dataList/OA-21778/A/1/datasetView.do); httpx advice to reuse clients (https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/ssl/). Building an httpx 0.28.1 AsyncClient took 135ms locally (measured).
- Benchmark scripts are in C:/Users/hennr/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-hennr-Desktop-NEXTSPOT/bb3f89c1-647b-4048-ad72-33f0ad33fdd6/scratchpad/ (bench_forecast.py, bench_matrix.py, bench_backtest.py, bench_batch.py).

findings.title: Public /area-demand/forecast amplifies arbitrary coordinates into DB RPCs and memory, and `_points_locks` grows without bound
findings.evidence:
- routers/area_demand.py:122-139: unauthenticated GET, no rate limit, lat 33-39 / lng 124-132, i.e. about 48M possible grid keys.
- area_demand_forecast_service.py:573: `_points_locks.setdefault(key, asyncio.Lock())` is never removed. `reset_points_cache` (179-189) is the only clear, and it is for tests only.
- Each new grid costs one RPC (56-day re-aggregation) plus up to about 1MB in `_points_cache`, evicting legitimate course grids (cap 96, line 137).

findings.cost:
- Measured 212B per distinct grid in `_points_locks`: permanent, attacker-controlled growth (for example 1M probes is about 200MB).
- Every probe also costs about 430KB of DB output and about 1MB of cache churn, and pushes useful grids out, so course latency goes back to cold. This is a cheap OOM/DoS lever against a 512MB single worker.
findings.proposal:
Short term (S):
- Replace the per-key lock map with an in-flight single-flight dict (`dict[key, asyncio.Future]`) whose entry removes itself in a `finally` block.
- Reject or short-circuit coordinates that are not within 2km of any known lot (the lot bbox is known from the store or the ITS facility cache) with `available=false`, before any I/O.
With the lot-matrix design, a request costs about 0.2ms and retains no memory, so no lock is needed.

findings.makes_unnecessary: `_points_locks` and the per-grid lock logic in `_load_points` (area_demand_forecast_service.py:568-581).

findings.title: The collection watchdog goes through the heavy-admin RSS shed and the reliability window query, so API memory pressure looks like 'collection down'
findings.evidence:
- .github/workflows/area-demand-alert.yml:57 polls `/api/v1/admin/area-demand-reliability?hours=6`.
- core/memory_guard.py:76-88 lists that path in `_HEAVY_ADMIN_PATHS`. The path-based gate runs before auth: at most 2 concurrent, a 503 shed at 400MB RSS (memory_guard.py:283-294), and a gc + malloc_trim after each call.
- area_demand_reliability_service.py:201-329 runs 3 parallel queries plus a lots query on every poll.
- GitHub API: the last 12 runs include 3 failures (2026-09-26 07:21Z exit 1; 12:51Z and 2026-09-27 01:14Z exit 22 = curl HTTP error after 3 retries). HANDOVER 09-26c confirms the 07:21Z run was a false alarm from a JSON parse of a 503 body.
- The 'hourly' cron (line 23) actually fired only every 3-6 hours (run timestamps).
findings.cost:
- About 25% false or ambiguous alerts, which trains people to ignore the only collection watchdog.
- The false alarms come exactly at high RSS, when the per-grid caches above are largest. The monitor and the memory problem are coupled.
- Every poll pays a full gc + malloc_trim and a DB window scan to answer a one-row question: 'is max(bucket_at) fresh?'.
findings.proposal:
Make the watchdog a data-plane check.
Option A (preferred): the workflow queries Supabase PostgREST directly with the service key already listed for Actions: `area_demand_snapshots?select=bucket_at&order=bucket_at.desc&limit=1`. That one indexed row catches every failure cause (API down, token mismatch, cron off) with zero dependency on API memory state.
Option B: the collector keeps an in-memory `collection_health` (last_success_at, last_error_code, consecutive_failures), updated in the collect handler and served as pre-serialized bytes from a tiny machine-token route that is NOT on the heavy list. After a restart it falls back to a single `max(bucket_at)` query.
Either way, parse JSON only on HTTP 200 and report non-200 as 'api_unreachable', distinct from 'stale'.
findings.makes_unnecessary:
- The watchdog's dependency on `/admin/area-demand-reliability` (that route can stay heavy for the admin panel).
- The JSON-parse-on-error failure mode.
- The `--retry-all-errors` loop masking shed 503s.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low. Monitoring only; no user-facing path changes. Option A needs `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` in Actions Secrets (human task in HANDOVER; record key names only).

findings.title: Calibration: `active_calibration` holds a threading.Lock across DB I/O, and the report rebuilds the Gyeongju shape with 26 PostgREST round trips on every view
findings.evidence:
- congestion_calibration_service.py:657-672: `with _cache_lock:` wraps `_build_state` -> `load_pairs` -> fetch_all_rows (network) while holding the lock.
- Callers wait on that lock while each occupies a pool thread: congestion_estimator_service.py:567 (to_thread), :626, and estimated_report_service.py:517-522 (admin I/O pool).
- :664-670: while the state is not applied (it is, because Seoul has 0 rows), it is refetched every 600s.
- `build_report` (:701-742, admin view, coalesced but not cached) calls `_load_gyeongju_levels` (:524-572): about 5 parent pages plus 21 `in_('snapshot_id', 200 UUIDs)` requests (URLs about 7.5KB each) for 28 days, to compute a capacity-weighted occupancy per bucket.
findings.cost:
- Stability: during a Supabase stall (HANDOVER records retry-transport stalls up to 120s on Linux), every estimator or report thread that needs calibration blocks on the lock. That exhausts the bounded pools shared with tourist traffic.
- Latency: 26 sequential round trips per calibration view (seconds from a US-region Render).

audit:I/O and runtime infra: core/su.subsystem: I/O and runtime infra: core/supabase.py transport+JWKS, postgrest_json, main.py executor/lifespan, ~200 thread-offload sites, deps/Dockerfile/render.yaml/uvicorn, logging, response serialization, GitHub cron jobs, TourAPI ingest (ingest.yml + scripts/ingest_tourapi.py + services/tourapi)
audit:I/O and runtime infra: core/su.summary:
Almost every runtime patch here (exclusive-connection transport, the 16-vs-8 executor debate, sys.setswitchinterval, the admin gate, the RSS shed, gc+malloc_trim, the warmup endpoint and cron) makes up for four root causes.

(1) The data layer is a sync supabase-py client run in a small thread pool. That pool is also used for DNS lookups (loop.getaddrinfo) and CPU work, and each call can hold a thread for 120 s (supabase.py:330-334). postgrest's own GET retry adds blocking sleeps of 1+2+4 s. So a Supabase brownout parks all 16 threads while /health stays green.

(2) Each request fans out several DB calls across the Pacific. /infrastructures makes about 16 Supabase requests in 4 sequential phases. Twelve of them are 150-id IN-list chunks whose IN-list is the whole active set, so the filter does nothing. render.yaml has no region, so the API is in Oregon (121 ms RTT to Seoul) rather than Singapore (69 ms).

(3) Warm-up is unbounded. The lifespan chain runs before the port opens with no overall time limit, and a best-effort GitHub cron (warmup.yml `*/10`) actually fires every 3-5 h.

(4) Global locks sit on the auth path. There is one RLock for JWKS, and an unknown `kid` triggers a network refetch, so anyone can stall authenticated traffic without logging in. There is also one asyncio.Lock for every user's profile-cache miss.

Measured locally:
- Starvation: with the shared 16-thread executor, DNS p95 was 406 ms, against 5 ms with an async pool of the same size. Throughput was the same (0.69 s vs 0.70 s), so the gain from async is isolating DNS and other work, not raw speed.
- Serialization is not the bottleneck. On 3.8 MB of synthetic map data: 36 ms with models + response_model, 31 ms with dicts, 5.4 ms with cached bytes. FastAPI 0.139 already serializes response_model with pydantic's `dump_json`. ORJSONResponse is deprecated and would switch that fast path off. Don't add GZipMiddleware: Render's load balancer already compresses with Brotli/gzip.
- `gc.collect` blocks the event loop even inside `to_thread`: a 145 ms stall at about 1.2 M tracked objects. After `gc.freeze()` a full collection took 0 ms.
- The runtime model is Ridge + one-hot. It could be a precompiled lookup table: bit-identical results, 0.13 µs vs 0.376 ms per call, and no sklearn/scipy import (2.65 s, +59 MB traced heap).
- The app's logging config emits httpx INFO lines containing the full URL, including the URL-encoded `serviceKey` for TourAPI, KMA, parking and Gyeongju food. An availability-chunk line is 6 KB.

TourAPI ingest:
- Slow because it awaits about 450 calls one by one: 89 rows × 4 detail calls, plus Kakao with a new TLS client per row. The TourAPI step took 147 s of a roughly 3.7 min job (GitHub run 36273753101).
- Flaky because of the US-runner → apis.data.go.kr network path (corroborated by an unrelated repo's report on the same day). The exit-75 re-dispatch chain works around this rather than fixing it. The cron also starts about 3 h late (21:40-22:21 UTC).
- Data loss is structural. postgrest-py sends `columns=` as the union of keys across the chunk and defaults missing keys to NULL, so a row whose detail calls failed gets overview, phone, homepage, operating_hours, barrier_free and gallery_images set to NULL. The same pattern means capacity is reset to the default daily and Kakao-corrected coordinates are reverted whenever Kakao fails.

Recommended order: S fixes first (timeouts/deadlines, async lock-free JWKS, per-user single-flight, drop the IN-list fan-out, ORDER BY in fetch_all_rows, lock file, bounded startup, `gc.freeze`, quiet httpx logs, uvicorn flags, ingest concurrency + incremental details). Then M: a snapshot publisher serving pre-serialized bytes with ETag/304 (keeping response_model so the OpenAPI snapshot is unchanged), the `ingest_tourapi_facilities` merge RPC, a Korean egress via an ap-northeast-2 Edge Function, moving to Singapore, and compiling the model. Then L: a native async PostgREST layer (AsyncPostgrestClient over one bounded httpx.AsyncClient — verified API-compatible and covered by the existing JSON patch), migrated module by module.

Sources: render.com/docs/blueprint-spec (region default oregon, immutable), render.com/docs/docker (automatic Brotli/gzip), docs.postgrest.org v12 preferences (missing → null), python-httpx.org/advanced/transports (retries only on ConnectError/ConnectTimeout), cloudping.co (p50 120.5/68.8 ms), github.com/Kludex/uvicorn/discussions/2939 (keep-alive race), github.com/KangseonLEE/irang/issues/140 (US runner ↔ data.go.kr timeouts on 2026-09-22), supabase.com/docs/guides/functions/regional-invocation.

findings.title: Supabase calls can park the shared 16-thread pool for 120 s each (plus postgrest's own blocking retry sleeps)
findings.evidence: core/supabase.py:330-334 httpx.Client(timeout=120): connect, read, write and pool timeouts are all 120 s. supabase.py:93,119-155 _STALE_RETRY_BACKOFF makes up to 3 attempts. postgrest 2.31 sync send_with_retry retries GET on 503/520 with time.sleep(min(2**n,30)) up to MAX_RETRIES=3, i.e. 1+2+4 s of blocking sleep inside the worker (site-packages postgrest/_sync/request_builder.py:37-55, base_request_builder.py:55,99-104). main.py:39 sets _IO_EXECUTOR_MAX_WORKERS=16, and that executor also serves loop.getaddrinfo for every httpx.AsyncClient (main.py:27-33). The web gives up after 4 s (map) or 10 s (api-client, supabase.py:34), but uvicorn does not cancel handlers on disconnect (memory_guard.py:245-247), so abandoned calls keep their threads. availability_service.py:44-48 already documents a 9 s Cloudflare 520.
findings.cost: A single Supabase brownout parks all 16 threads for tens of seconds. Every tourist DB call and every new outbound connection's DNS lookup (LLM, Kakao, KMA) then queues behind them, while async /health stays green so Render never restarts the instance. Local benchmark (server with 120 ms latency; 3 map-shaped loads of 16 parallel calls + 20 single calls + 10 DNS lookups): DNS p95 406 ms on the shared 16-thread executor vs 5 ms with an async pool.
findings.proposal: Now: give the Supabase client httpx.Timeout(connect=3, read=12, write=5, pool=2). Reads longer than the web's own 10 s timeout are wasted work. Turn off postgrest's internal sleep-retry on request-path queries (.retry(False)). Wrap each request-path DB call in asyncio.timeout(deadline) so abandoned work stops. Batch scripts get a separate client with long timeouts.
findings.makes_unnecessary: Part of the executor-sizing reasoning (main.py:23-39); thread-occupancy worries behind the admin gate.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low. Only failure timing changes. Long admin aggregates need an explicit per-call timeout, or should move to the bulk lane or snapshot.

findings.title: JWKS: one global lock plus refetch on unknown kid lets an unauthenticated caller stall all authenticated traffic
findings.evidence: core/supabase.py:260-273 _get_signing_key holds the module-global _jwks_lock (RLock) around get_signing_key_from_jwt for every token. PyJWT 2.13 PyJWKClient calls get_signing_keys(refresh=True), i.e. a new urllib TCP+TLS fetch, whenever the token's kid is unknown, and also every 300 s (lifespan default). The timeout is 2 s plus one retry (supabase.py:36-37,253-256,271-273). The kid comes from the unverified header, so a forged ES256 header (supabase.py:405-406) triggers a network fetch while the lock is held. get_current_user is a sync dependency (supabase.py:430), so waiters occupy anyio's 40-token threadpool. 27 endpoints use Depends(get_current_user) directly, and get_current_profile/require_role (authz.py:168) resolve through it. That pool's saturation already caused 483 of 509 /health checks to exceed 5 s (tests/test_import_footprint.py:24-29).
findings.cost: Each bogus-kid request costs one serialized JWKS round trip: about 0.4-0.5 s Oregon→Seoul including TLS, up to 4.2 s when it fails. A few such requests per second stall logins and the admin and merchant consoles (the 'bounce' symptom). The normal-path CPU is negligible: PyJWKSet.from_dict 10 µs + ES256 decode 53 µs (measured).
findings.proposal: Make auth async and lock-free. Keep an in-process {kid: key} snapshot refreshed by a background task every 10 min (stale-while-revalidate; keep the last good set on failure). An unknown kid triggers at most one single-flight refetch per 60 s; otherwise answer 401 immediately. Verify on the event loop and make get_current_user `async def`. Fetch through the shared async httpx client with keep-alive.
findings.makes_unnecessary: _jwks_lock and _JWKS_RETRY_BACKOFF; asyncio.to_thread(verify_supabase_token) at authz.py:214 and account.py:736; the JWKS warmup step (main.py:122-129).
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low. Same keys, claims and leeway. Key rotation is still handled by the rate-limited refetch, which also answers the HANDOVER's pending worry that limiting unknown-kid refetches would 401 during key rotation.

findings.title: The profile-cache lock is global: every user's cache miss waits behind other users' DB round trips
findings.evidence: authz.py:60 _cache_lock = asyncio.Lock() is one lock for all users. authz.py:139-151 holds it across _load_profile: a users query plus, for merchant/developer, a facility_owners query (authz.py:79-102), each via to_thread with the 120 s client timeout. TTL is 30 s (authz.py:56), so each active user misses about twice a minute.
findings.cost: Head-of-line blocking across users. With N users expiring together, the Nth waits for up to 2N sequential round trips (20 users ≈ 2.3-4.6 s at 121 ms RTT) even when Supabase is healthy. During a brownout every user inherits the slowest query, which fits the /account/me 10 s-timeout incident class.
findings.proposal: Per-user single-flight: a dict of user_id → asyncio.Future, with no global lock. Load role and owned facility ids in one round trip (RPC or view returning role + array_agg(facility_id)). Bound the load with asyncio.timeout(3), which still maps to today's 503.
findings.makes_unnecessary: _cache_lock
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low; same TTL and the same degraded/503 contract.

findings.title: Replace the sync client in threads with one native async PostgREST client and a bounded pool
findings.evidence: About 201 thread-offload sites by AST count: 177 asyncio.to_thread + 26 run_admin_io/run_in_executor. About 158 wrap DB calls and 43 wrap CPU work. By module: dev.py 26, admin.py 25, account.py 16, recommendations.py 14, merchant.py 13, parking_derived_congestion 8, infrastructures.py 7, coupons/reports/predict/feedback 6 each. The following plumbing exists only so a sync client can survive threads: _ExclusiveConnectionTransport, _StaleConnectionRetryTransport and SEND_HEADERS message matching (supabase.py:45-245); 64 idle transports × 2 clients (supabase.py:172); the 16-worker executor (main.py:23-62); the ADMIN_IO pool (executors.py:40,69,92-94); setswitchinterval (main.py:41-46). Verified: postgrest 2.31 AsyncPostgrestClient accepts http_client=httpx.AsyncClient (postgrest/_async/client.py:38,97) with the identical builder, `await db.table(...).select(...).eq(...).execute()` and `.rpc()`, and the existing postgrest_json patch applies to it (MockTransport run showed _JsonLoadsAdapter in use).
findings.cost: The thread hop itself is only ~50 µs. The real costs: (a) DB, DNS and CPU work share one 16-thread bulkhead (see the timeout finding's measurement); (b) about 250 lines of concurrency plumbing behind 4 incident classes in 30 days (HPACK race, EBADF, duplicate POST, SEND_HEADERS-closed); (c) threads multiply glibc arenas. With the pool capped at 16, throughput is identical (0.69 s vs 0.70 s in the benchmark), so the win is isolation and simplicity.
findings.proposal: Add app/core/db.py with two AsyncPostgrestClients (anon, service_role) over ONE httpx.AsyncClient(http2=False, Limits(max_connections=16, max_keepalive_connections=16, keepalive_expiry=15), Timeout(3/12/5/2), transport=AsyncHTTPTransport(retries=1)). Per httpx docs, retries=1 retries only ConnectError/ConnectTimeout, which is safe for POST. Reserve lanes with asyncio.Semaphore(4) for admin/aggregate/snapshot builds. Add an async fetch_all_rows twin. Codemod `await asyncio.to_thread(X.execute)` → `await X.execute()` module by module, starting with authz, infrastructures, recommendations and courses. Keep the sync client for scripts/ and the two auth-admin calls (account.py:839, dev.py:141). CPU work gets an explicit 2-worker pool (run_heavy). Replace MagicMock chains (75 test files, 270 refs) progressively with an httpx.MockTransport fake PostgREST that serves both the sync and async clients.
findings.makes_unnecessary: supabase.py:45-245 transports and message matching; ADMIN_IO pool; most of the ~158 DB to_thread wrappers; executor sizing beyond DNS; likely setswitchinterval once CPU work is precomputed.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Medium-high regression surface. Mitigate with a dual stack, per-module migration, and re-running the 09-26 WSL chaos harness against the async stack. Large bodies now parse on the loop (a 1.17 MB json.loads ≈ 10-15 ms on the desktop), so keep big reads off the request path (snapshots) or parse them via run_heavy.

findings.title: TourAPI ingest overwrites good data with NULLs, default capacity and reverted coordinates
findings.evidence: ingest_tourapi.py:258-261 bulk-upserts chunks of 100 rows with heterogeneous keys. postgrest 2.31 pre_upsert adds columns= as the union of keys (site-packages postgrest/base_request_builder.py:107-110,186-188) and default_to_null=True. PostgREST docs: omitted keys are written as null, and the conflict update covers the listed columns. extract_detail_common omits empty keys by design (transform.py:259-283), and enrich_row swallows per-call failures (ingest_tourapi.py:163-196). So a row whose detail call failed gets overview/phone/homepage/operating_hours/barrier_free/gallery_images set to NULL. transform_poi always sends image_url (None when the list has none) and capacity=CAPACITY_DEFAULTS (transform.py:133,135), so admin capacity edits (admin.py:116) are reset daily. When Kakao reconcile fails (kakao_coordinate_service.py:95-96), TourAPI coordinates overwrite the previously Kakao-corrected ones while the merged features still say coordinate_source=kakao (ingest_tourapi.py:251-254). The features merge is a client-side read-modify-write (ingest_tourapi.py:232-254) that races merchant.py:526-539.
findings.cost: Silent data loss on exactly the days the network is flaky, map markers flip-flopping between two coordinates, and provenance that lies. The fallback path also issues one UPDATE per row (ingest_tourapi.py:282-288).
findings.proposal: Add one idempotent SQL function, ingest_tourapi_facilities(rows jsonb): INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (contentid) WHERE contentid IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET name=excluded.name, overview=COALESCE(excluded.overview, facilities.overview) (same for phone/homepage/operating_hours/barrier_free/gallery_images/image_url/address), capacity=facilities.capacity (default applies on insert only), latitude/longitude kept when features->>'coordinate_source'='kakao' and this run did not re-match, features = facilities.features || excluded.features (atomic, no pre-read). This needs a new migration, RESET regen and a PRELUDE DROP entry. The script sends only keys it actually obtained. Interim fix without a migration: group rows by frozenset(keys) and upsert per group; strip None image_url and the capacity key for existing contentids.
findings.makes_unnecessary: The features pre-read (ingest_tourapi.py:232-254) and the SELECT→INSERT/UPDATE fallback (263-290).
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low-medium. Review SECURITY INVOKER/RLS for the function and add a SQL test for the COALESCE semantics.

findings.title: No dependency pinning, plus a monkeypatch of private postgrest internals and error-string matching
findings.evidence: requirements.txt:7-18 is entirely >= constraints, and Dockerfile:9 re-resolves them on every Render build; CI does the same. postgrest_json.py:53-59 replaces the private base_request_builder.JSONAdapter. If upstream renames it, install() just warns and returns False (postgrest_json.py:56-58), and the pydantic parser that cost +56.7 MB RSS on a 2.87 MB page (postgrest_json.py:3-8) silently returns. supabase.py:85-88 matches the substrings 'ConnectionState.CLOSED' and 'SEND_HEADERS'. FastAPI behaviour is version-dependent: 0.139 serializes response_model via pydantic dump_json (fastapi/routing.py:704-726). AGENTS.md already notes a realtime/websockets mismatch.
findings.cost: Prod behaviour can change on any deploy without a Python change, the OOM mitigation can regress silently, and CI and prod can resolve different versions.
findings.proposal: Generate a hashed lock file (uv pip compile or pip-compile → requirements.lock) and use it in the Dockerfile, CI and the ingest job, with a weekly Dependabot/Renovate PR to move it deliberately. Add a test asserting postgrest_json.install() is True and JSONAdapter is _JsonLoadsAdapter, and log the patch state at boot. After the async layer lands, parse PostgREST bodies directly instead of patching.
findings.makes_unnecessary: The HANDOVER's open 'pin/upgrade httpx/httpcore' item.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Very low; it freezes the currently tested set.

findings.title: Lifespan startup is an unbounded serial chain that runs before /health can answer
findings.evidence: main.py:107-178 runs these steps in order before uvicorn serves requests: start_model_manager (registry query + Storage download + unpickle, no timeout; predict_service.py:170-174), JWKS (2 s), fetch_all_facilities (paged, 120 s client timeout), current_estimates (no timeout), area context (the only step with a cap, 12 s). Every step swallows errors, but none bounds time.
findings.cost: After an OOM restart (8 in 5 days) that coincides with Supabase slowness, the API is unreachable for the whole chain, minutes in the worst case, and Render health checks fail. The boot also piles up heap that memory_guard later has to trim.
findings.proposal: Open the port immediately. Lifespan only builds clients and schedules the snapshot scheduler; endpoints serve last-known-good or a labelled degraded response (503 + Retry-After for the first seconds). Wrap any remaining boot step in asyncio.timeout(5). Call gc.freeze() after the first successful build.
findings.makes_unnecessary: The ordered warm steps in main.py:131-173.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low-medium. The first seconds after boot may serve degraded data, which must be labelled per AGENTS.md.

findings.title: memory_guard's gc.collect stalls the event loop even when run in a thread
findings.evidence: memory_guard.py:141-160 release_memory runs gc.collect() then malloc_trim(0). It is called via asyncio.to_thread after admin bursts (memory_guard.py:263-269), in the preflight (memory_guard.py:289) and after warmup (warmup.py:227). gc.collect is a single C call that holds the GIL. Measured: with ~1.2 M tracked objects (600k synthetic dict/list rows; gc.freeze reported 1,204,905 frozen), gc.collect inside to_thread took 145 ms and the event loop's longest tick gap was also 145 ms; the same heap after gc.freeze() took 0.0 ms. malloc_trim via ctypes releases the GIL.
findings.cost: Every admin burst or warmup pauses all requests, /health included, for a full-heap collection. On 0.5 CPU this is likely 2-4× the desktop figure.
findings.proposal: Keep malloc_trim (GIL-free) but drop gc.collect from the request path. Call gc.freeze() once after boot snapshots are built so long-lived caches and the graph are never traversed again. Move static data into non-GC containers (numpy/array CSR, per the walking-graph idea). Keep the RSS shed only as a last resort.
findings.makes_unnecessary: Most of the burst accounting and preflight-trim logic (memory_guard.py:196-294).
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low; gc.freeze is stdlib (3.7+) and objects created later are collected normally.

findings.title: The stale-connection retry can re-send writes the server already committed
findings.evidence: supabase.py:117-155 retries ANY method on ReadError/RemoteProtocolError (supabase.py:49-61). Over HTTP/1.1, a disconnect or read reset after the body was fully written means an insert may already have committed. HANDOVER 2026-09-26c lists this path as still open.
findings.cost: Rare duplicate congestion, availability or tracking rows. Two identical reports can look 'corroborated', which corrupts the evidence tiers.
findings.proposal: Make retries phase- and method-aware. Retry anything whose failure came before bytes were sent (ConnectError, ConnectTimeout, PoolTimeout, SEND_HEADERS-closed). After bytes were sent, retry only GET/HEAD, PostgREST upserts (resolution=merge-duplicates), and inserts carrying a client-generated primary key with resolution=ignore-duplicates, which are idempotent by construction. This is about 30 lines around AsyncHTTPTransport in the async layer.
findings.makes_unnecessary: The blocked 'V4' retry patch discussion.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low-medium. Some POSTs that currently 'succeed on retry' will surface as errors until they get client ids, so audit reports.py, tracking.py and coupons.

findings.title: fetch_all_rows paginates with OFFSET and no ORDER BY (28 callers)
findings.evidence: supabase.py:356-386 uses .range(start, start+page_size-1) with no order. There are 28 call sites and only about 4 add an order; the ingest ones do (ingest_tourapi.py:240,377). facilities has 1,682 rows, so the map always needs at least 2 pages (infrastructures.py:268-270).
findings.cost: Postgres guarantees no row order without ORDER BY. An UPDATE between the page-1 and page-2 requests (merchant.py:539, admin edits, ingest, is_active sync) creates a new tuple version that can cross the page boundary, so a facility is duplicated or missing for that request. Pages are also fetched sequentially (+1 RTT each).
findings.proposal: Default fetch_all_rows to order by primary key with keyset pagination (id=gt.<last>&order=id). Fetch the remaining pages concurrently when a count is known. This fixes all 28 callers in one place.
findings.makes_unnecessary: Per-caller .order() workarounds.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low; the primary-key index already exists.

findings.title: GitHub cron is best-effort: warmup.yml and area-demand-alert fire every few hours, and the monitor hits a heavy admin endpoint
findings.evidence: warmup.yml:13 is scheduled '*/10' but has only 39 runs in total; the recent ones are 3-5 h apart (GitHub API). area-demand-alert.yml:23 is hourly but its runs are 3-6 h apart, and 3 of the last 10 failed. It curls /api/v1/admin/area-demand-reliability (area-demand-alert.yml:54-57), which is in _HEAVY_ADMIN_PATHS (memory_guard.py:84): gated to 2 concurrent and shed with 503 above 400 MB (memory_guard.py:283-294). That gives false alarms exactly when the box is busy, which HANDOVER 09-26c confirms. The instance is actually kept awake by pg_cron every 10 min (HANDOVER:22-24).
findings.cost: The 'kept warm every 10 min' guarantee doesn't hold. The alert is noisy and depends on the health of the very instance it monitors. Each /warmup rebuilds caches that then need trimming (warmup.py:224-227).
findings.proposal: Delete warmup.yml and /warmup once in-process snapshots exist. Monitor freshness without touching the Render instance: read area_demand_snapshots?select=bucket_at&order=bucket_at.desc&limit=1 from PostgREST with a read-only key, or add a 1-row cached GET /area-demand/freshness. Treat non-JSON responses as 'unknown', not 'down'.
findings.makes_unnecessary: warmup.yml, routers/warmup.py (~230 lines) and its release_memory call.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low.

findings.title: Ingest flakiness comes from the US runner → apis.data.go.kr network path; the exit-75 re-dispatch chain works around it
findings.evidence: ingest.yml:15-25 attributes the failures to the first locationBasedList2 hitting a 10 s timeout on some runners. ingest.yml:217-240 re-dispatches up to 2 fresh runners. Run 35788265971 died 10 s into the TourAPI step. An unrelated repo reported US runner ↔ data.go.kr timeouts the same day (KangseonLEE/irang#140, 2026-09-22). The cron '0 19 * * *' (ingest.yml:37) actually started 21:40-22:21 UTC over the last 6 runs, about 3 h late (06:40-07:20 KST).
findings.cost: About 1 in 4 runs dies before doing any work. The workaround brings complex workflow logic and operator rules ('never press Re-run').
findings.proposal: Give data.go.kr calls a Korean egress. Deploy a small Supabase Edge Function pinned to ap-northeast-2 (x-region / forceFunctionRegion) as an allowlisted GET proxy. It injects serviceKey from function secrets and requires the service token. Point BASE_URL (tourapi/client.py:28) at it via env for the ingest, and optionally for the runtime festival/weather/parking calls from Render. Alternatively, pg_cron can trigger the ingest as that function. Keep the list retry, drop the fresh-runner chain, and move the cron off :00 (e.g. '23 18 * * *').
findings.makes_unnecessary: The retry-on-fresh-runner job, EXIT_TEMPFAIL plumbing and operator rules (ingest.yml:26-32,217-240; ingest_tourapi.py:82-92,456-463).
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Medium: a new moving part that must not become an open proxy (endpoint allowlist + token). The free quota of 500K invocations/month is far above ~400/day.

findings.title: httpx INFO logs every outbound URL, leaking query-string API keys and 6 KB IN-lists
findings.evidence: logging.py:29-33 calls basicConfig(level=INFO) on the root logger, so httpx's 'HTTP Request: GET <full url>' lines are emitted. Only the Seoul key is redacted (seoul_citydata_service.py:190-196). Keys sent as query params: tourapi/client.py:80-86, tourapi/insights.py:25, weather_service.py:104, parking_demand_service.py:339, gyeongju_restaurant_service.py:288. Verified with the app's setup_logging: 'HTTP Request: GET https://apis.data.go.kr/.../detailCommon2?serviceKey=abc%2B%2Fdef%3D%3DSECRET&contentId=1'. The key is URL-encoded, so exact-match maskers miss it. A 150-id chunk line is 5,992 bytes. structlog JSONRenderer (logging.py:49) escapes Korean, and stdlib lines are plain text alongside the JSON lines.
findings.cost: Keys end up in Render logs whenever events, weather, parking, live-detail or search call out. About 72 KB of log per map load. User UUIDs from eq.user_id filters also land in the logs.
findings.proposal: Set the httpx and httpcore loggers to WARNING. Emit an own structured db_call line (table, status, ms, rows; no URL). Add a serviceKey/authKey redaction filter as defense in depth. Route stdlib records through structlog.stdlib.ProcessorFormatter and use JSONRenderer(ensure_ascii=False). Human task: rotate keys that may already sit in log history.
findings.makes_unnecessary: The Seoul-only redaction special case.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Very low.

findings.title: Replace request-time fan-out, TTL caches and warmup with one in-process snapshot publisher serving pre-serialized bytes with ETag/304
findings.evidence: /infrastructures builds 1,682 pydantic models per call with no cache (infrastructures.py:370-436). Lifespan (main.py:92-178) and /warmup (warmup.py:163-202) rebuild caches that expire. ResponseCache deep-copies on store and on every read (response_cache.py:137,179,185). The web polls the full map every 3 min (useCongestionAlerts.ts:30). Measured with FastAPI 0.139 on 1,682 synthetic rows (3.8 MB): models + response_model 36 ms; dicts + response_model 31 ms; orjson bytes 8 ms; cached bytes 5.4 ms (the transport floor). deepcopy of a 0.8 MB list takes 9 ms vs orjson.loads 3 ms. FastAPI 0.139 already serializes via pydantic dump_json (routing.py:704-726). ORJSONResponse is deprecated (responses.py:70-81) and would disable that fast path.
findings.cost: Serialization is about 1% of the 2.7-4.2 s TTFB. The real cost is the ~16-call DB fan-out repeated on every request and poll, 17-25 MB of transient heap per call, and trans-Pacific transfer of 1.17 MB pages.
findings.proposal: Add a generic Snapshot primitive (bytes, etag, built_at, parsed view) and ONE scheduler task in lifespan that rebuilds each snapshot on its cadence and swaps atomically: the static map layer on a version bump from ingest or admin writes, the live congestion overlay every 60 s, festival/weather every 10 min. Builds use the bulk lane. Handlers return Response(snap.bytes, headers ETag + Cache-Control: max-age=30) and answer If-None-Match with 304. Keep response_model= in the decorators: returning a Response bypasses validation (routing.py:696-699), so tests/contracts/openapi.snapshot.json stays unchanged. Do NOT add GZipMiddleware; Render's load balancer already applies Brotli/gzip and in-process gzip would burn the 0.5 CPU. Cache bytes, not object graphs. Payload slimming belongs to the facility-cache workstream.
findings.makes_unnecessary: routers/warmup.py + warmup.yml; lifespan warm steps (main.py:131-173); ResponseCache deepcopies; the web's 4 s fallback to direct Supabase reads; ~16 Supabase calls per map request.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Medium. Make staleness explicit (etag and built_at in the payload) and never let a snapshot build overlap itself.

findings.title: The Render service is in Oregon while the DB and users are in Korea
findings.evidence: render.yaml:6-12 has no region:, so the Blueprint default is 'oregon', and region cannot be changed after creation (Render blueprint spec). Supabase is in Seoul. AWS p50 latency (cloudping.co): us-west-2↔ap-northeast-2 120.5 ms, ap-southeast-1↔ap-northeast-2 68.8 ms. /infrastructures has at least 4 sequential DB phases, courses/plan makes ~20 area-demand RPCs, and new connections add TCP+TLS round trips.
findings.cost: About 52 ms saved per sequential round trip: at least 0.2 s on the map path, more on cold connections and slow-start-bound 1 MB transfers. Korean users save about 50 ms per API call. Shorter in-flight time also means fewer overlapping requests and a lower peak RSS.
findings.proposal: Human task: first confirm the actual region in the Render dashboard. Then create the service with region: singapore, copy the env, switch the web's API base URL, and retire the old service. Ideally do this together with the snapshot work.
findings.makes_unnecessary: Part of the latency-driven timeout inflation.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low-medium (URL/env cutover).

findings.title: TourAPI ingest is slow: about 450 sequential awaits, and unchanged details are re-downloaded daily
findings.evidence: GitHub run 36273753101 (09-26): TourAPI step 147 s, Kakao discovery 20 s, Gyeongju 21 s, pip install 19 s. ingest_tourapi.py:486-487 awaits enrich_row row by row, and each row makes 4 sequential calls (detailCommon2/Intro2/Info2/Image2, 155-196) plus an optional Wikimedia call. With 89 contentid rows that is ~356 detail calls, roughly 0.3 s per sequential await. The Kakao loop is sequential (ingest_tourapi.py:491-494) and opens a new httpx.AsyncClient (new TLS) per row (kakao_coordinate_service.py:74), which makes its Semaphore(5) (line 12) moot. Detail calls have no retry (ingest_tourapi.py:85; client.py:61-65). The job pip-installs the whole runtime (sklearn/scipy/pyproj) (ingest.yml:91).
findings.cost: About 2.5 min per run and ~356 quota calls per day for content that rarely changes. Every extra call is another chance to hit the flaky network path.
findings.proposal: (a) Incremental details: list items carry modifiedtime. Store it in features.tourapi_modifiedtime and fetch details only when it changed, when details are missing, or when they are older than 7 days, typically 0-15 calls/day. (b) Cap in-flight calls at 4 with an asyncio.Semaphore; gather each row's 4 detail calls; use one shared AsyncClient; retry transient errors (TransportError/5xx/429) twice with 1-3 s jitter. (c) For Kakao, use one shared client and gather, and skip rows that already have kakao_place_id unless name or address changed. (d) Use a requirements-batch.lock. Expected: TourAPI step about 15-25 s, whole job about 1 min.
findings.makes_unnecessary: The 15-minute step-timeout budget reasoning (ingest.yml:94-99).
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low. Keep at most 4 calls in flight to stay under any per-second limit.

findings.title: The runtime loads scikit-learn and SciPy to evaluate a Ridge over one-hot features
findings.evidence: The model is Ridge + OneHotEncoder on 3 categorical features (scripts/train.py:21-23,68-72; predict_service.py:97-110 checks len(categories_)==3). Unpickling it imports sklearn and scipy. Measured on the desktop: importing sklearn.linear_model + preprocessing on top of numpy takes 2.65 s and +59 MB traced heap; a single-row predict takes 0.376 ms. The precompiled table (intercept + 3 dict lookups) takes 0.13 µs and was verified bit-equal. main.py:96-101 records a first unpickle of 18.8 s in prod. predict_congestion is offloaded to threads at 8+ sites.
findings.cost: Tens of MB RSS whenever a model is active, multi-second boot and refresh CPU, pickle.load of downloaded bytes, and a heavy image.
findings.proposal: At train time, emit a JSON artifact of about 2 KB: {intercept, per-feature coefficient tables, categories, schema_version, metrics}. Predict at runtime with dict lookups (unknown category contributes 0, matching handle_unknown). Keep the sha256 check and registry contract. Move scikit-learn to requirements-train.
findings.makes_unnecessary: The pickle path; predict_congestion to_thread wrappers (predict.py ×5, recommendations.py, courses.py, merchant_briefing ×2, score.py); sklearn/scipy in the image.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Low-medium. Add a test that compares the table against the pickled model over the full category grid.

findings.title: uvicorn and Docker runtime flags
findings.evidence: Dockerfile:32 runs sh -c 'uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8080}'. That means --timeout-keep-alive defaults to 5 s, shorter than typical proxy idle timeouts (the half-closed socket 502 race, uvicorn discussion #2939); there is no exec, no --timeout-graceful-shutdown, and FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS stays at its 127.0.0.1 default. App .py files are not byte-compiled into the image: import took 4.27 s with a cold bytecode cache vs 0.92 s warm (desktop, all modules), and compiling app/ takes 0.23 s. No PYTHONUNBUFFERED is set for the service or the ingest job.
findings.cost: Possible sporadic 502s on reused load-balancer connections, slower restarts after OOM on 0.5 CPU, lost print() lines when an ingest step times out, and lifespan shutdown skipped on a hard kill.
findings.proposal: Use CMD ['sh','-c','exec uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port ${PORT:-8080} --timeout-keep-alive 75 --timeout-graceful-shutdown 20 --no-server-header']. Add RUN python -m compileall -q app after COPY, and ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 (also in ingest.yml). A non-root USER is already on the security list.
findings.makes_unnecessary: None.
findings.stability_risk_of_change: Very low.

design.target_architecture:
ONE PRINCIPLE: shared reference data is read into the process once per data version, never once per request. Everything a request needs is already in memory, as an immutable snapshot or as pre-serialized bytes. The database answers only user-specific reads and writes, and aggregates it can compute itself (returned as one JSONB). This retires the patch layer: the gate, RSS shed, gc+malloc_trim, coalescers, the HEAVY/ADMIN_IO pools, warmup, deep copies and the 4 s race. Nothing is left to protect.

====================================================================
TARGET ARCHITECTURE (3 planes, 1 owner per datum)
====================================================================

```
                 Supabase Postgres (Seoul) ── the single durable truth
   facilities, facility_source_refs, congestion_logs, availability, timesales,
   area_demand_snapshots(+_lots), forecasts, model_registry, users/...
   [P5] admin_* / merchant_stats / impact_rollup / safety_latest_levels RPCs (1 jsonb each)
   [P5] estimated_bucket_rollups (written by the 10-min collect), calibration_state
        ▲ 60s probe + keyset loads          ▲ user rows only           ▲ 1 RPC per admin panel
        │ (ONE build thread)                 │ (auth profile, persist)  │
 pg_cron 10' ─POST collect─┐                 │                          │
 ┌─────────────────────────▼─────────────────┴──────────────────────────┴───────────┐
 │ FastAPI, 1 uvicorn worker (Render 512MB / 0.5 CPU)                                  │
 │                                                                                     │
 │ REFERENCE PLANE  app/services/reference_snapshot.py  (sole owner of shared state)   │
 │   Refresher task (lifespan) + 1-thread build executor "nextspot-ref"                │
 │   Source(name, load, every_s, probe, backoff 5→300s, last-good, atomic swap)        │
 │   ├ FacilityBase   v=blake2b(rows)  all_rows/active/by_id/grid + baked priors,     │
 │   │                per-facility precompute (graph snap, hours bitmask)            │
 │   ├ LiveOverlay    v, next_flip_at  latest congestion rows, corroborated avail,    │
 │   │                active timesales (is_current/is_stale evaluated at flip time)  │
 │   ├ ParkingHistory v=last bucket   [P2] lot×time uint16 matrix, 56 d, ~0.3MB       │
 │   ├ Forecasts/Priors(date), IndustryBaseline, Calibration(v), JWKS{kid:key}        │
 │   ├ PredictTable(model_v)  [P3] 672 cells, no sklearn in the request path          │
 │   └ WalkingGraph   [P3] CSR arrays baked into the Docker image at build time       │
 │   Artifacts (bytes + ETag=blake2b(body), rebuilt per version, never per request):   │
 │     /infrastructures (canonical + REGION.bounds + LRU 4), /congestion/estimates,   │
 │     [P7] /infrastructures/map, /detail/{id}, /area-demand/curve                    │
 │   mark_dirty(source) from every in-process writer (1s debounce); out-of-process     │
 │   writers bounded by the 60s probe (count + max(updated_at), trigger-maintained).   │
 │                                                                                     │
 │ REQUEST PLANE  handlers: snap = reference_snapshot.current() ONCE per request       │
 │   GET map/estimates → Response(prebuilt bytes) or 304; 0 DB calls, 0 thread hops   │
 │   reco/by-type/course → pure-CPU candidate pipeline over snap                       │
 │     (route from precomputed snaps → evidence → area demand from matrix → score.py  │
 │      UNCHANGED) → 1 batched insert for persistence                                  │
 │   auth: JWKS snapshot on the loop; per-user single-flight profile cache             │
 │                                                                                     │
 │ WRITE PATH  collect handler: persist → ParkingHistory.append → publish lots to      │
 │   parking cache → estimator recompute → estimates bytes → [P5] bucket rollup        │
 └─────────────────────────────────────────▲──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                           │ ETag/304; one request per screen
                     Web (Vercel static export): [P7] lib/mapData.ts (IndexedDB + version),
                     no Supabase-direct map reads, visible-tab polling only, no prefetch
```

OWNERSHIP: one module owns each datum, and each datum has one refresh rule.

| Datum | Owner | Refresh rule |
|---|---|---|
| Facilities + source attribution | reference_snapshot.FacilityBase | Loaded with keyset `order=id&id=gt.` pagination through the same anon client as today, so RLS visibility is unchanged. Rebuilt on the 60s probe, on mark_dirty (admin.py:128,148,165; dev.py:666; search.py:463-475; merchant.py:539), at KST midnight and as a 15-min backstop. The version is a content hash, so a rebuild with no change keeps the same ETag, even across OOM restarts. |
| Measured congestion | LiveOverlay | 60s, plus mark_dirty (reports.py:271, admin.py:237, infrastructures.py:675, merchant.py:598), plus the exact 30-min is_current and 24h is_stale flip instants. One rule, congestion_evidence.measurement_is_current. |
| Availability | LiveOverlay | One query for the whole corroborated, unexpired set, with no IN-lists; flips at expires_at. mark_dirty from reports.py:184. |
| Timesales | LiveOverlay | Active rows only; flips at starts_at and ends_at. mark_dirty from merchant.py:309,359,379. |
| Parking history, current lots, estimates | parking_history + estimator | Appended by the 10-min collect (routers/area_demand.py:150-158). The separate live ITS fetch runs only when the last collect is more than 5 min old. |
| Area-demand forecast | Derived from ParkingHistory at the exact coordinate | Arithmetic copied verbatim from aggregate_nearby_points (area_demand_forecast_service.py:229-280). Memo keyed by (grid, version). |
| Model predictions | PredictTable | Built per cell when the model activates, so results are bit-exact. |
| Admin KPIs | Postgres RPCs | Computed on each call. Python aggregators are kept only as test oracles. |

INVARIANTS:

P2 contradicts itself on determinism. It says `_load_points` computes the series 'at the exact requested coordinate' with arithmetic 'verbatim' and calls itself a 'determinism fix'. blocking_issues: B1 (P1/P3): the plan bakes time-dependent correctness into cached bytes, but a request never checks whether those bytes have expired. Evidence: is_current is a 30-min window (congestion_evidence.py:43-67). is_stale is 24 h (infrastructures.py:36,60-74). Availability expires_at is checked at read time (availability_service.py:23-41). Estimates are re-aged to 60 min at export time (congestion_evidence.py:145-181), and the comment there says this was added after a red-team finding that a cache served 65-min-old parking as 'now'. The plan only recomputes these at `next_flip_at`, from ONE refresher that shares the single I/O thread with every load. A load stuck on Supabase makes the flip late: 20 s read timeout under P0a, plus postgrest's sleeps between retries, times attempts. If the refresher task dies from a bug, flips stop for good. Either way /infrastructures keeps serving is_current=true and /congestion/estimates keeps serving expired estimates. That is exactly the regression estimate_for was written to prevent. Fix: each artifact carries `valid_until = next_flip_at`. The handler checks `now < valid_until`; otherwise it recomposes on a CPU-only path from the raw overlay rows, which needs no I/O and does not queue behind a load, or it serves available=false. Also run the refresher loop under a supervisor that catches per iteration and restarts, and add a staleness alert.

B2 (P1, made worse by P7): if Supabase is unreachable at boot there is no last-good snapshot, and backoff still grows 5→300 s. After Supabase recovers, the map, estimates and (after P3) recommendations and courses can keep returning 503 for up to 5 minutes. Today the next request recovers at once. Boots are frequent: 8 OOM restarts in 5 days, plus every deploy. Fix: while nothing has ever been built, cap backoff at about 10-15 s and let an incoming request kick an immediate attempt, rate-limited. Apply the long backoff only when a last-good exists.

B3 (P2): ParkingHistory will silently get permanent holes on normal deploys. Render keeps the old instance serving until the new one is healthy (render.com/docs/zero-downtime-deploys). If pg_cron's 10-min collect (area_demand.py:141-158) lands on the old instance during that overlap, the bucket is persisted to the DB but appended only to the old process. The new instance already did its boot load, and the next collect advances `version = last bucket_at`. The tail-sync rule `bucket_at > version` therefore never refetches the missed bucket, and the (grid, version) memo never invalidates. Area demand drifts from the RPC oracle until the next restart. Fix: tail-sync over a trailing window (e.g. last 2 h) and merge idempotently by bucket_at; the record RPC already returns stored=false for an existing bucket (20260824120000:163). Make version include a count or content hash, and add a periodic reconciliation of bucket counts.

B4 (P0b as written, which ships now): 'retry GETs on 503/429 honouring Retry-After' reverses a lesson learned in production. api-client.ts:280-281 says retrying 429/503 caused a retry storm that got the Cloudflare IP blocked, and that this was observed live. Restricting the network-error retry to GETs also removes the Cloudflare Managed-Challenge mitigation (api-client.ts:108-112, 227-230) from the POST paths: /recommendations, /by-type and /courses/plan. With a shared judge network, one IP block takes down every judge. Fix: keep 'never retry on a response status' for now. Keep the single 700 ms pre-response retry for POSTs until P4's scoped X-Request-Id idempotency exists. Change only the 'no retry after a client timeout' part, which is already the current behaviour.

B5 (P7, and P4's publicGet): deploy ordering. Vercel and Render both auto-deploy from the same main push (HANDOVER.md:9), and Render's Docker build is minutes slower. It also fails independently, for example if the new `--emit-bin` build step breaks. The new web would then call /infrastructures/map, /area-demand/curve, /recommendations/board and /admin/dashboard/bundle before they exist, and P7 deletes the Supabase fallback (main/page.tsx:575-743) at the same time. Web code must fall back to the legacy endpoints on 404/5xx. B6 (P4): JWKS is made a reference_snapshot Source on the same single 'nextspot-ref' thread. Its boot load then queues behind FacilityBase, LiveOverlay and the 9-page ParkingHistory boot load, and any hung load blocks key refresh. Every authenticated request, /account/me included, fails during boot or brownouts. Separately, 'unknown kid → refetch at most once per 60 s, otherwise 401' is the exact risk the team deferred (HANDOVER.md:250: '키 교체와 겹치면 401'). adminGate treats a 401 as a negative verdict and redirects to login (apps/web/lib/adminGate.ts:12,50), so a key rotation would bounce admins and judges. missed_opportunities: Console-style row fragments: at base build, pre-serialize each row once as its own JSON bytes (without congestion and availability), plus small per-facility overlay fragments. Any filter or LRU variant then becomes `b'[' + b','.join(frags) + b']'`, which is only memcpy, with no pydantic on the loop. A flip re-encodes only the rows whose is_current or is_stale changed, not the whole 1.37 MB body. It also removes the attacker-controlled rebuild cost.

Row-level patch on mark_dirty: after an admin or merchant write, fetch only `id=eq.<id>`, splice it into a copy-on-write snapshot and bump the version. That makes the change visible in about one round trip, so the writing handler can even await it for read-your-writes (FacilityTable refetch after create, seat broadcast). No 2 MB reload per click.

Replace the count+max(updated_at) probe with one trigger-maintained `reference_versions(name, v bigint)` row, bumped by statement-level triggers on facilities, facility_source_refs, congestion_logs, facility_availability_reports and merchant_timesales. The probe becomes exact: no transaction-start watermark miss, catches trigger-inserted congestion rows, and needs no aggregates. It is also already multi-worker-safe (plan invariant 5), and removes the need for the 15-min backstop.

Serve `valid_until`: emit `Cache-Control: private, max-age=<seconds to next flip, capped>` alongside the ETag. Repeat loads inside the window then cost zero network, and the server-side validity check (B1) and the client agree on one expiry.

Make the map survive API outages: have the refresher, or the 04:00 ingest, publish the canonical facility bytes plus ETag to a Supabase Storage public object on the Seoul CDN. The web uses it as the IndexedDB seed and as the fallback when Render is restarting, instead of the buggy direct-table fallback. It also lets a cold-boot 503 degrade gracefully.

Snapshot sanity gate: refuse to swap in a FacilityBase whose active count drops more than X% from last-good unless a known in-process writer marked it dirty, or two consecutive loads agree. This guards against a bad ingest day, RLS or schema-cache hiccups, or an empty page being treated as truth for the whole process.

Separate the executors by failure domain instead of 'one build thread': a CPU-only compose lane (flips and artifact bytes, never blocked on I/O), a DB-load lane for reference loads, and a fast lane for auth keys. Builds within a lane still never overlap, but a slow load cannot delay correctness flips or authentication.
